doc.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Davern's tone and playing; the Dialogues record
summary: They discuss Davern's tone and the coming record with Ken Peplowski and two guitars.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: He had a certain legato tonguing style on his instrument I really, really like. And I just am always amazed at his inventiveness with creating melodies, which is what I like to hear in an improviser.

Yeah, right, exactly, exactly. To him tone was extremely important. He always strove to get the best clarinet tone that he could. He didn’t believe in a lot of notes, he believed in choosing the notes carefully that he wanted to play but to play them well and to play them in tune and with the proper sound. He liked rhythm.

Well in this record that I mentioned, that will be coming out soon, which will be called “Dialogues” with Ken Peplowski, we have James Chirillo and Howard Alden, two guitars, no piano. Two guitars, bass and drums.
